<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 198.99966. Assuming this is a potassium adduct ([M+K]⁺), subtracting the mass of K⁺ (38.963707 Da) gives a neutral mass of ≈160.036 Da. The formula C₆H₈O₅ matches this neutral mass (exact mass 160.0372 Da) within a few ppm, making it the most plausible molecular formula.</thought>
<final_answer>C6H8O5</final_answer>
